title: Sep 30 Results + Oct 1 Preview: A Split Decision Kind of Day
summary: We went 2-2 on Sep 30, but here's why tomorrow's Braves pick feels different

content.value:
## Here's the Thing About .500 Days

September 30th gave us exactly what none of us want but all of us experience: a perfectly split day. Two wins, two losses, 50% accuracy. It's the kind of result that makes you shrug and say, 'well, at least we're honest about it.'

The Braves and Astros both let us down with 62% confidence picks that didn't pan out. But the Yankees and Padres came through right when we needed them to. That's baseball—sometimes your strongest reads miss, and your coin-flip calls hit.

## What We Learned From the Misses

The Braves loss stings a bit because we're going right back to that well tomorrow. Sometimes the model sees something in the matchup that takes more than one game to play out. The Astros miss? That one's easier to digest—Houston's been unpredictable lately, and 62% was probably generous.

But those two wins keep us grounded. The Yankees at 50% was essentially us saying 'this could go either way,' and it went our way. The Padres pick felt solid at 62%, and they delivered. That's the kind of validation that keeps the confidence intact.

## Tomorrow's Top Pick: Back to Atlanta

Here's where it gets interesting. Our top pick for October 1st is the Atlanta Braves again—same matchup, Phillies at Braves. Aaron Nola takes the mound for Philadelphia against Ray Kerr for Atlanta.

The confidence is slightly lower at 57%, which feels more honest given what happened yesterday. But the underlying numbers still favor Atlanta at home. Sometimes you have to trust the process even after a miss, especially when the fundamentals haven't changed.

content.title: ⭐ Oct 1 Top Pick
content.sub: 57% win probability · Nola vs Kerr · Home advantage

content.value:
## The Pitching Matchup

Aaron Nola is a veteran presence who knows how to navigate tough lineups, but Ray Kerr at home gives the Braves an edge the model likes. It's not a blowout projection—57% says this game could easily swing either way—but there's enough there to make Atlanta the smarter play.

After yesterday's split, tomorrow feels like a chance to prove the process works over time. One game doesn't define a system. Two games in the same matchup? Now we're building a story.

Let's see if the Braves can deliver what they couldn't on September 30th. Sometimes the second chance is the one that matters most.

author: Hana
